title: Randomized Trial of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Heart Failure
rawText:
TITLE: Efficacy of Dapagliflozin in Patients with Heart Failure and Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.

METHODS:
In a multi-center randomized controlled trial involving 4,800 patients with HFpEF (LVEF >= 45%), participants were assigned to Dapagliflozin 10mg daily (n=2,400) or placebo (n=2,400) alongside standard therapy. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure event over a median follow-up of 2.3 years.

RESULTS:
The primary outcome occurred in 385 patients (16.0%) in the Dapagliflozin group compared to 468 patients (19.5%) in the placebo group (Hazard Ratio 0.82; 95% CI, 0.72 to 0.94; p=0.003). All-cause mortality was not significantly reduced (p=0.12).

CONCLUSION:
Dapagliflozin significantly reduces the risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure in patients with preserved ejection fraction.

fabricatedClaims.claim: Dapagliflozin reduced all-cause mortality by 45% with high statistical significance (p < 0.001).
fabricatedClaims.contradictionReason: Source document explicitly states all-cause mortality was not significantly reduced (p=0.12).

title: Meta-Analysis of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Chronic Kidney Disease
rawText:
TITLE: Renal Outcomes with GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of 7 Landmark Trials.

BACKGROUND:
GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetes, but their cumulative impact on renal progression requires pooled quantification.

RESULTS:
Across 7 major trials comprising 56,004 patients, GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy reduced the composite kidney outcome (macroalbuminuria, doubling of serum creatinine, 40% eGFR decline, or kidney replacement therapy) by 17% (HR 0.83; 95% CI, 0.78 to 0.89; p < 0.0001). Macroalbuminuria incidence alone was reduced by 24% (HR 0.76; 95% CI, 0.70 to 0.83).

CONCLUSION:
GLP-1 receptor agonists confer substantial renal protective benefits in patients with type 2 diabetes.
